title: How to Grill Brie Cheese on a Mat for an Elegant Appetizer
meta_description: Learn how to grill brie on grill mat for a gooey, melted appetizer. Discover the best tips for non-stick results and elegant pairings in this guide.
html:
There is something magical about melted Brie. Its buttery, creamy texture makes it the ultimate crowd-pleaser, but grilling it can be a nerve-wracking experience. If you've ever tried putting a wheel of soft cheese directly on grill grates, you know the struggle: the cheese leaks out, sticks to the metal, and creates a giant flare-up that chars the rind. That's why the secret to a perfect, gooey result is to grill brie on grill mat.

Using a non-stick barrier allows you to get those beautiful grill marks on the outside while the center turns into a molten pool of gold, all without the mess. Whether you're hosting a summer garden party or a cozy fall gathering, this appetizer feels high-end but takes less than ten minutes to pull together.

Why Use BBQ Grill Mats for Brie?

Brie is a delicate cheese. Unlike Halloumi, which has a high melting point, Brie is designed to soften and flow. When you place it on bare grates, the cheese inevitably seeps through the gaps. Not only do you lose half your appetizer to the coals, but the dripping fat causes flames that can burn the cheese in seconds.

This is where BBQ Grill Mats come into play. These reusable non-stick mats act as a protective shield. They distribute the heat evenly and prevent the cheese from sticking or leaking. You get the smoky flavor of the grill and the aesthetic of charred rind, but with total control over the process. Plus, cleanup is a breeze—you just wipe down the mat instead of scrubbing charred cheese off your grill grates.

Ingredients and Tools You'll Need

To keep this appetizer elegant and balanced, you want a mix of salty, sweet, and acidic flavors. Here is what I recommend gathering before you head outside:

  • One 8oz wheel of Brie: Look for a double-cream or triple-cream Brie for maximum meltiness. Keep it chilled until the moment you grill it; this helps the rind hold together longer.
  • Fresh Herbs: Thyme or rosemary sprigs work beautifully.
  • Honey or Fig Jam: For a sweet glaze.
  • Crusty Baguette: Sliced into rounds and lightly toasted.
  • Fresh Berries or Apple Slices: For a tart contrast.
  • BBQ Grill Mats: To ensure a non-stick, flare-up-free experience.

Step-by-Step: How to Grill Brie on Grill Mat

The goal here is a warm, molten interior and a lightly toasted exterior. Follow these steps for the best results:

1. Preheat Your Grill: Set your grill to medium heat (around 350°F to 400°F). You want a steady heat, not a scorching flame, to avoid burning the rind before the center melts.

2. Prepare the Mat: Place your BBQ Grill Mats directly on the grates. If you're grilling bread at the same time, you can use a separate mat or a different section of the grill.

3. Prep the Cheese: Gently pat the Brie wheel dry with a paper towel. If you want extra flavor, you can lightly score the top rind in a crosshatch pattern, but don't cut too deep, or the cheese will leak faster.

4. The Grill Process: Place the Brie wheel directly on the mat. Close the lid and let it grill for about 3 to 5 minutes. You aren't looking to flip it; you just want the bottom to toast and the heat to penetrate the center.

5. The Finish: Once the cheese feels soft to the touch (give it a gentle poke), remove it from the grill using a wide spatula. Immediately drizzle with honey or a dollop of fig jam while it's still piping hot.

Serving Suggestions for an Elegant Presentation

The way you present grilled Brie is what turns it from a snack into an "elegant appetizer." I suggest placing the melted wheel on a wooden charcuterie board or a slate platter. Surround the cheese with your toasted baguette slices, fresh apple wedges, and a handful of walnuts or almonds for crunch.

For an extra touch of sophistication, garnish the top of the cheese with a sprig of fresh thyme and a sprinkle of flaky sea salt. The salt cuts through the richness of the cream, making the flavors pop. Serve it immediately—Brie is best enjoyed while it's still molten and gooey.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your Grill Mats

One of the best parts about using BBQ Grill Mats is that they are reusable. After your Brie is served, let the mat cool down completely. Since Brie is fatty, you might have some residue left behind. Simply wash the mat with warm, soapy water and a soft sponge. Avoid using metal scrubbers, as you want to preserve the non-stick surface for your next session of grilling delicate foods.

FAQ

Can I grill Brie on a mat if I'm using charcoal instead of gas?

Yes! BBQ Grill Mats work perfectly on charcoal grills. Just make sure your coals are spread evenly and you've reached a medium temperature before placing the mat and cheese down to avoid hotspots.

What if my Brie starts to melt too quickly?

If the cheese begins to flow out of the sides too fast, your grill is likely too hot. Move the mat to a cooler part of the grill (indirect heat) and close the lid. This allows the heat to circulate and melt the center without scorching the bottom.

Can I add toppings before grilling?

I recommend adding glazes like honey or jam after grilling. If you put sugar-based toppings on the cheese while it's on the grill, they can burn or caramelize too quickly, potentially sticking to your mat or creating smoke.
